stem:
Om fills a closed plastic syringe with air and seals the nozzle with his finger. When he pushes the plunger, the air occupies a smaller volume.

Which claim best explains why the air can be compressed?

options.text: Air particles have large empty spaces between them, so pushing the plunger brings the particles closer together.
Each air particle itself shrinks in size when the plunger is pushed.
Air is a continuous solid block with no spaces, so the plunger cannot change its volume.
Air behaves like an incompressible liquid, so its volume stays fixed when the plunger is pushed.

teacher.key_rationale: Gases can be compressed because large empty spaces separate their particles; the plunger reduces those spaces without shrinking the particles themselves.
